title: Sensex Gains 362 Points as Fed's Waller Signals Pause, but Weekly Losses Mount
excerpt: Indian benchmarks snap a four-session losing streak after Fed Governor Christopher Waller's dovish comments, though crude oil concerns and Middle East tensions cap gains.
body:
• The BSE Sensex closed 362.57 points (0.48%) higher at 76,515.43 on Friday, September 4, snapping a four-session losing streak after Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller signaled support for keeping rates steady.
  • Smallcap indices hit fresh intraday lifetime highs, though the Sensex and Nifty both posted their fourth consecutive weekly decline — the longest losing streak in five months.
  • Brent crude jumped about 7% for the week on intensifying U.S.-Iran hostilities, keeping broader risk sentiment cautious despite the Friday relief rally.
  • Market-implied odds of a September Fed rate hike fell to roughly 50% from 63% after Waller's comments, though a strong U.S. jobs report later Friday pushed expectations back toward 62%.

Indian equity markets snapped a four-session losing streak on Friday as comments from Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller eased concerns over an imminent U.S. rate hike, though elevated crude oil prices and Middle East tensions kept gains in check.

The BSE Sensex closed 362.57 points, or 0.48%, higher at 76,515.43 after surging as much as 730 points to an intraday high of 76,883.14. The Nifty 50 settled 24.25 points, or 0.10%, up at 23,897.70, having touched 24,005.75 during the session before profit-taking trimmed the advance.

Fed Pause Narrative Drives Relief Rally

The catalyst for Friday's gains came from Washington. Waller told Reuters NEXT on Thursday that he would support keeping the federal funds rate in the 3.50%-3.75% range if upcoming inflation data shows price pressures are moderating. The comment shifted market-implied odds of a September rate hike from above 63% to roughly even.

Goldman Sachs economists said in a note that they expect the Fed to keep rates unchanged, "though a hike is possible if the CPI and PPI come in higher than we expect." The CPI report is due September 11, with the Fed's next meeting scheduled for September 15-16.

The dovish signal helped push global bond yields lower and supported equities across Asia. U.S. markets had closed sharply higher overnight, with the Dow Jones gaining 624 points.

Smallcaps Shine, but Weekly Pain Persists

The session's standout was the broader market, where smallcap indices registered fresh intraday lifetime highs on stock-specific buying driven by strong earnings momentum and domestic demand. Nifty Metal was the top sectoral gainer, rising more than 1%, while financial services shares also advanced.

On the losing side, Nifty IT fell 0.47%, while pharma and healthcare indices declined 0.68% and 0.87%, respectively, reflecting a rotation away from defensive sectors toward cyclicals.

Despite Friday's rebound, both benchmarks posted weekly losses of about 1-1.2%, marking their fourth consecutive weekly decline — the longest losing streak in five months.

Crude Oil Remains the Central Overhang

Brent crude jumped roughly 7% during the week as intensifying U.S.-Iran hostilities stoked inflation fears and drove global bond yields higher.

"Crude remains the market's central overhang, leaving investors wary of the near-term outlook. Even strong domestic growth data and GST collections have struggled to lift sentiment meaningfully this week."

— Samrat Dasgupta, CEO, Esquire Capital Investment Advisors

The India VIX fell 6.24% to 10.63, signaling reduced near-term volatility expectations, while the rupee firmed slightly to 94.48 on fresh FCNR deposit inflows.

What's Ahead

The relief rally faces an early test. The U.S. August employment report released later Friday showed stronger-than-expected job creation, pushing market-implied odds of a September rate hike back toward 62%. Capital Economics analysts noted that "even the most committed dove would struggle to find anything in the August employment report to justify keeping interest rates unchanged."

The coming week brings U.S. producer price data on September 10 and consumer inflation on September 11, followed by the Fed's September 15-16 meeting — a trio of events that will likely determine whether markets extend the relief rally or resume their retreat. A busy IPO pipeline could also divert flows from secondary markets.
